AM7I-01.solved: 0.15 x 80 = 12. Stem asks for the reduction, not the new price.
AM7I-01.note: 68 is the sale price, 92 is a 15% increase, 15 is the bare percent. Clean single-step percent-of. Template T1 (see note on AM7I-03/04/09/12).

AM7I-02.note: 86 is the median, which is a real wrong path; 83 and 87 correspond to no derivation I can construct - they are near-misses padding the set.

AM7I-03.note: 24 = the markup alone, 36 = 60% of 60, 100 = adding 40 instead of 40%. Good distractor set. Same habit as AM7I-01.

AM7I-04.note: 144 = the other 60%, 40 = the bare percent, 200 is loose. Third consecutive single-multiply percent item.

AM7I-05.note: 20 and 15 are the two means-ish reads, 29 = 14+15. This is the simplest member of the mean-total-recovery template (T2) shared with AM7I-13, AM7I-23 and AM7I-28.

AM7I-06.note: 24 = the area, 160 = perimeter(20) x 8, 80 = ? weakly motivated. Straight area-then-multiply.

AM7I-07.note: 175 = 35% of 500 (the intended error), 300 = stopping after step one. Nominally a percent-of-a-percent, but the stem sequences it for the student, so the two ideas never actually collide - it reads as two consecutive multiplications. Medium, not hard.

AM7I-08.solved: Eight values already in order; median = (6+8)/2 = 7.
AM7I-08.note: 5 = the mode, 6 = the lower middle value, 7.5 = mis-averaging 6 and 9. The list is pre-sorted, which removes the only real obstacle in a median item.

AM7I-09.note: 2.52 = the tax alone, 33.48 = subtracting it, 43 = adding 7 dollars. Fourth single-step percent item; see the template note in my summary.

AM7I-10.solved: 30/15 = 2 h and 30/10 = 3 h, so 60 miles in 5 h; 60/5 = 12 mph.
AM7I-10.note: Genuinely hard by the stated test: the student must recognise that speeds do not average, and the total-distance/total-time idea has to interact with the two legs. 12.5 is the mean of 15 and 10 and is the whole point of the item. Best item in the batch.

AM7I-11.note: 81 = 27 x 3, 12 = 4 x 3 (treating it as a linear conversion), 31 = 27+4. One multiplication.

AM7I-12.note: 30 = 27/90, 40-ish = green share mis-read, 25 = guessing a quarter. Requires forming the total first, which is the only wrinkle.

AM7I-13.solved: 25 x 78 = 1950 total; morning 10 x 90 = 900; afternoon total 1050; 1050/15 = 70.
AM7I-13.note: Hard: the mean<->total conversion has to run in both directions and the two subgroup totals have to be combined. 66 = 78-12 and 84 = the midpoint-ish guess are exactly what a student who averages the means produces. Shares template T2 with 05/23/28 but is the only member where the weighting bites.

AM7I-14.note: 21 = the red beads, 7 = one part, 15 = 3 x 5. Textbook part-to-whole ratio.

AM7I-15.note: 200 = stopping early, 235 = coupon first only, 188 = taking 20% off (250-15). Two steps but strictly sequential - no interaction, so medium.

AM7I-16.note: Hard, and for the right reason: the added cashews change BOTH the part and the whole, so the two quantities interact. 25 is what you get treating the whole as fixed (0.5x50 = 25, minus nothing), 15 = half of 30, 10 = the current cashews. Second-best item in the batch.

AM7I-17.note: 25 = one face, 15 = 3 x 5, 60 = total edge length (12 x 5), which no student produces when asked for volume. One formula recall.

AM7I-18.solved: 9 x 15 = 135 on adult tickets; 195 - 135 = 60 on student tickets.
AM7I-18.note: 6 = the NUMBER of student tickets rather than the dollars - a real and well-placed trap on a careless reader. 135 = adult spend, 90 = 9 x 10. The trap is the only thing lifting this above trivial.

AM7I-19.note: 58 = adding the first 8 minutes (answers the wrong question), 70 = 700/10 ignoring the first leg, 28 = 20+8. A rate that changes partway, but the stem hands over the structure in order, so the student never has to see the interaction - it decomposes into three one-line steps. Medium.

AM7I-20.note: 48 = stopping at tablespoons, 4 = 64/16, 12 = 48/4. Two conversions chained; routine on the real exam.

AM7I-21.note: Hard: successive percent changes compose multiplicatively AND the chain has to be inverted. 1020 x 1.05 style errors give 969 (= 1020 x 0.95) and 1200; 850 = 1020/1.20. Third genuinely hard item.

AM7I-22.solved: Counts 2,5,6,8 sum to 21, so the median is the 11th value. Cumulative: 2, 7, 13, 21 - the 11th falls in the '2 siblings' column. Median = 2.
AM7I-22.note: TABLE CHECKED AND CONSISTENT. The SVG's two rows are labelled 'Number of siblings' (0, 1, 2, 3) and 'Number of students' (2, 5, 6, 8); the frequencies sum to 21, matching the stem's '21 students', and each value sits inside the column rule it belongs to (cell boundaries 170/209/248/287/328 against text anchors 189.5/228.5/267.5/307.5). No disagreement between the table and its labels. 1.95 is the MEAN (41/21 = 1.952) and is the strongest distractor here; 1.5 is the midpoint of the sibling labels, 3 is the modal-ish top column.

AM7I-23.note: Nearest miss to hard in the batch: mean and median have to interact. It falls short because x lands above every known value, so the median is the middle of the four given numbers regardless of x's exact size. 22 = answering with x, 14 = the mean, 16.5 = averaging 13 and 20. Same T2 opening as 05/13/28.

AM7I-24.note: 16.80 = the overage alone, 76.80 = charging all 640 at 0.12 plus 35 (well, 640x0.12 = 76.80 exactly - that is the no-allowance error and it is a good one), 111.80 = both. Structurally the same shape as AM7I-19: a fixed leg plus a per-unit leg.

AM7I-25.solved: 2 cm = 6 m, so 1 cm = 3 m. Garden is 21 m by 27 m; area = 567 sq m.
AM7I-25.note: 63 = the drawing's area in sq cm, 126 = 63 x 2, 96 = (7+9) x 6 - the weakest of the three. Converting both lengths first is the obvious route and it dissolves the scale-factor-squared idea entirely, so the two ideas never have to interact. Medium, though it is the item most likely to be mislabelled hard.

AM7I-26.note: 1750 = using W = 25 (forgetting to halve correctly), 8400 = 70 x 120, 4200 = 70 x 60. Recovering a dimension from the perimeter is one small idea on top of a formula.

AM7I-27.note: 9.09 = dividing by the NEW wage (the classic base error, well chosen), 1.85 = the raw difference, 110 = the ratio. Two steps, base chosen once.

AM7I-28.note: 3.40 = answering with the mean, 4.00 = a guessed round-up, 5.80 = 2.60+3.20. Solved by the identical habit as AM7I-05 and the opening of AM7I-13 and AM7I-23: total = n x mean, then subtract the knowns.
